title: Consolidate fallback telemetry and add proactive capacity throttles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a regional capacity spike on 2026-02-20 we observed repeated cross-region reroutes and rapid model-variant switches that produced customer-facing latency spikes and a short outage window. Root cause analysis shows three contributing issues: (1) fragmented fallback telemetry across router shards made it impossible to detect replaying reroute loops quickly, (2) policy propagation was non-atomic leading to transient policy states, and (3) there was no soft throttling at the router level to prevent rapid fanout when downstream capacity dipped. This ticket consolidates telemetry, introduces proactive capacity throttles and damping heuristics, and tracks runbook and test-harness changes required to prevent recurrence.
action_items: Consolidate fallback/variant decision telemetry into a single shardable timeline stream (telemetry team) — owner: Priya Rao — due: 2026-03-17
Add per-region soft capacity throttles at the router to limit fanout rate when backend pool health degrades (serving runtime) — owner: Marcus Nguyen — due: 2026-03-21
Introduce fallback damping window: suppress repeated variant flips for the same request trace for 5s by default (routing logic) — owner: Liam Chen — due: 2026-03-18
Make policy propagation atomic by adding a config-version handshake and fast-path rollback on partial apply (control plane) — owner: Zoe Martinez — due: 2026-03-24
Add circuit-breaker telemetry and alerting for reroute storm patterns (observability) — owner: Daniel Kim — due: 2026-03-15
Create a deterministic chaos test in staging that simulates sudden pool exhaustion and verifies throttle + damping behavior (SRE/QA) — owner: Hannah Wu — due: 2026-03-20
Update runbooks & call trees to include immediate fallback-to-stable-variant policy and manual throttle override steps (ops) — owner: Asha Patel — due: 2026-03-12
Ship a canary rollout of throttles+damping to 10% of traffic and monitor prefix key KV-collision and latency regressions (release) — owner: Liam Chen — due: 2026-03-26

resolution_summary: Work in progress. Early staging tests show significant reduction in variant flip frequency and fanout during simulated capacity loss. Full mitigation requires coordinated rollout of telemetry consolidation and router soft-throttles. Canary planned; will observe for policy propagation regressions and KV collision side-effects.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: conservative throttling reduces peak throughput and may increase queued latency for some customers, but prevents widespread variant churn and downstream p99 spikes.

Rollback plan: disable soft throttle and revert damping flag via config-version rollback. If policy propagation shows increased latency, revert atomic handshake temporarily and engage control-plane for hotfix.
Post-deploy verification: monitor new telemetry stream for reroute-loop signatures, observe customer-facing latency and error rate for 48h post-canary.
